text: When a program doesn’t work as expected, the first step is to identify the bug. This means reproducing the problem and figuring out where things go wrong. Instead of guessing, a systematic approach works best: break the code into smaller parts and test each one. Many programmers rely on debugging tools, which let you pause the program and inspect variables step by step. Another useful technique is logging, or adding print statements, to track what the program is doing at certain points. By combining these methods, you can find the root cause more quickly and fix it without creating new issues.
